title: Hipparcos (1990-93) phases agree with TESS (2018-26) rotation ephemerides for 144 of 165 magnetic Ap/Bp stars; seven stars keep 0.1-0.23 cycle offsets that ASAS-3 cannot assign to period change
abstract: Question: Do magnetic chemically peculiar (Ap/Bp) stars keep a constant rotation period for 30 years? Method: From the Netopil et al. (2017) list, 259 magnetic CP stars show a strong rotation signal in Hipparcos epoch photometry (1989-1993). For 241 of them we fit TESS light curves (SPOC 2-min and TESS-SPOC FFI, 2018-2026) with a Fourier template and a linear ephemeris. We fit the template to the Hipparcos data and measure the phase offset (O-C) after 509 to 21,600 rotations. We accept in-phase and inverted solutions because the Hp and TESS bands differ. ASAS-3 V data (2000-2009) give a third epoch for 108 stars. Results: 165 stars pass the bridging criteria. 144 agree with a constant period; their core scatter is 0.031 cycles and does not grow with the number of cycles, so it is most probably a passband or shape offset. The median 3-sigma limits are |P_TESS - P_mean| < 4.9 s, |dP/P| < 2.3e-5 and P/|Pdot| > 0.69 Myr. The mean Pdot/P of the sample is +0.027 +- 0.030 per Myr. The control 56 Ari gives Pdot = 2.4 +- 0.8 s per century, as published. The published spin-down of BS Cir does not appear in the phases. Seven stars (HD 15089, HD 19712, HD 39575, HD 41251, HD 49333, HD 125903, HD 141641) keep offsets of 0.10-0.23 cycles with all TESS sectors; as period changes these would have time scales of 0.3-1 Myr. ASAS-3 shows that four of them are also outliers in 2005, but its calibration slope against Hipparcos (0.32 +- 0.05) is near the constant-Pdot value, so it cannot separate period change from band offsets. Limitations: band-dependent light-curve shapes, a Gaussian-core threshold, ASAS-3 saturation for bright stars, and two TESS sectors for HD 19712. display.caption: Hipparcos O-C against the TESS ephemeris for 165 bridged mCP stars, against the number of rotation cycles (left), and the normalized offsets with a unit Gaussian (right). Grey: constant period; orange: offsets above 3 sigma in both phase metrics; aqua: offset in one metric; blue: known period-change stars 56 Ari (HD 19832) and BS Cir (HD 125630).

Multi-epoch O-C (Hipparcos 1991, ASAS-3 about 2005, TESS sectors) for candidates and BS Cir, with constant-Pdot and static-offset reference curves, and the ASAS-3 against Hipparcos calibration for 72 constant-class stars (slope 0.32).
Hipparcos data folded on the TESS ephemeris with the TESS template at the predicted phase (blue) and at the best-fit shift (orange) for the two controls and seven candidates.

Uses the ASAS-3 cgi download and light-curve loading rules (grades, aperture choice, time conversion).
Netopil et al. (2017) list of CP stars with rotation periods: source of the sample.
Mikulasek (2016) review of mCP period changes, including the BS Cir spin-down that our phase data do not show.
Adelman et al. (2001) 56 Ari period increase; our Hipparcos-TESS phase gives a consistent Pdot.
